Double-buffer shared-memory setup, insert, and read functions with alignment and magic checks.

# Purpose
This file implements the public API for a shared-memory double buffer in `fd_dbl_buf`. It provides functions to report the required alignment and memory footprint, create and initialize a buffer in shared memory with [`fd_dbl_buf_new`](<#fd_dbl_buf_new>), attach to an existing buffer with [`fd_dbl_buf_join`](<#fd_dbl_buf_join>), detach with [`fd_dbl_buf_leave`](<#fd_dbl_buf_leave>), and invalidate the buffer with [`fd_dbl_buf_delete`](<#fd_dbl_buf_delete>). The code checks for `NULL` pointers, alignment errors, and a magic value in `fd_dbl_buf_t` before it accepts a shared-memory region as valid.

The file also provides data transfer operations for the double buffer. [`fd_dbl_buf_insert`](<#fd_dbl_buf_insert>) copies a message into the next buffer slot, limits the message size to the configured MTU, and updates the sequence and size fields with memory fences to control visibility across threads or processes. [`fd_dbl_buf_read`](<#fd_dbl_buf_read>) repeatedly calls `fd_dbl_buf_try_read` until it gets a valid result, which gives a blocking read interface on top of the lower-level read attempt. The code uses SSE support when `FD_HAS_SSE` is enabled to update sequence and size together with a single 128-bit store.
